lessons: In consume, when replaying an already-journaled decision, run the release hold-discard and mutate(request) only if decision.request.lifecycle == self.lifecycle. Otherwise unlink the file and return the decision without mutating.
A restart creates a new lifecycle through uuid4, so a leftover file from a crash between the journal append and the unlink must never act on the new lifecycle's state or its hold set.

Add a test to tests/test_control.py: publish and accept under lifecycle A, raise inside mutate, then build a new ControlInbox with lifecycle B on the same journal and state dir. Call consume and assert that mutate is not called, no hold is discarded, and the file is gone.

Keep the existing structure: journal-first decisions, conflict and invalid handling, crash-safe publication tests and the control_consumer hook all passed review. Fix only this one finding and stay inside the four fenced files.
reason: The only review snag is a fixable replay-across-restart oversight with a concrete paved road, and all mechanical checks passed.
